scene: The door of Room 150

Warm flat-illustration of a high school classroom: one teen at a desk looks politely confused, small question marks above their head, hand starting to rise, diverse classmates working; hopeful mood, no text in image.” Normalize confusion on day 4, on purpose. Today we learn what to SAY when we're lost

Flat illustration, warm colors: two diverse teens greeting each other in a bright school hallway with lockers, two large EMPTY speech bubbles above them, no text anywhere in the image.” The empty bubbles preview today's mini-dialogue. Take 3–4 student versions and read them aloud

A warm 2×3 grid of six diverse high-school student portraits (East African, Central American, Middle Eastern, Southeast Asian, Haitian, Afghan), each with a small home-country flag below, flat illustration, friendly, no text.” Bridge from Week 1: we described ourselves; now we describe PEOPLE. Fish for 'he' and 'she' in student answers

Flat illustration, top-down view: an open teen backpack with items arranged around it — notebook, pencils, smartphone, charger, keys, small family photo, granola bar — bright colors, no text.” The family photo in the image is deliberate — it seeds 'I have a family' language without forcing anyone's story

Flat illustration: teen with a smartphone held like a microphone playfully interviewing another teen, colorful question marks floating above, school setting, energetic, no text.” Play up the celebrity-interview angle — today everyone is famous for 3 questions
Room 150 — our room

Flat illustration of a classroom desk scene with five identical orange cats: one inside an open backpack, one on the desk, one under the chair, one next to a laptop, one peeking from behind a stack of books — cute, clean, no text.” Cats because cats win. Five positions in one image = the whole lesson previewed

A friendly flat illustration of an open toolbox with six labeled slots; slot 1 glows golden with a small speech-bubble icon, slots 2–6 are gray silhouettes; warm colors, celebratory, no text except the number 1.” Self-assessment disguised as a Do Now.
